text: Mac Gréine was an Irish god and the husband of Ériu, the earth goddess who gave her name to Ireland. With his brothers Mac Cécht and Mac Cuill he formed a trio of parallel gods. Their wives were land goddesses. His name means son of the sun. The word for sun is feminine in Irish, so scholars read the name as a matrilineal title, not proof of an ancient solar god. Mac Gréine did not carry his father's name. He was, like his brothers, a son of Ogma, the god of eloquence. The warrior poet Amairgin of the Milesians killed him.
